problem.target_statement: Determine irrationality of the rational-base Lambert values, with 3/2 as the first resistant explicit base.
problem.claim_ceiling: The published Bundschuh-Vaananen theorem plus the kernel-checked specialization establishes irrationality at 7/2, while 3/2 remains outside the recorded published regions and open. Exact q-Apery work excludes natural-prefix compression and opens moving-tail modular compression. The stored modular-only selector pairs fail the normalized analytic consumer at starts 1 through 4, while an analytic-aware unimodular recombination repairs that consumer exactly at starts 0 through 3 and preserves rank two. The huge recombination heights are substantially structural: Lean proves |Delta| <= 2 H epsilon (|B_0|+|B_1|), and the exact start-3 data force at least 1874 coefficient bits for the certified common ceiling. Lean also proves that at a rational target a/q one of two non-collinear integral forms has size at least 1/q, so generic continued-fraction cofinal decay is not an independent lemma but already entails irrationality. New tail-denominator arithmetic finds long source-supported odd divisor runs and a matching extra Plucker index, but exact block-aligned losses for 5, 7, 13, 19, 23, 29, and 97 refute fixed-prime infinite-tail promotion. Lean proves that a finite-window common denominator divisor reduces binary pigeonholing to one coordinate and that a prime occurring once in the determinant forces a rational 1/q gap. The surviving q-Apery producer was recorded as a cofinal moving-prime law rather than an infinite fixed tail; that reading is now CORRECTED - Wolstenholme refutes only a tail starting at the first-appearance index j=d, and past the LAST loss block a fixed prime does persist: J_5={4,20,24} is finite by descent, so 5 divides B_j for every j>=50 and the step-1 window divisor is cofinal unconditionally, with no input from Boyd; finite subunit forms do not establish irrationality. For every outward Van Assche evaluation m_n>=n, the exact coefficient degree, target-tail cutoff, and forced homogeneous rational clearing give positive main term (n*m+n^2/2)log(4/3)+(3/pi^2)m^2 log 3. This closes evaluation choice and denominator cancellation as scalar repairs, but not primitive common content. The adjacent second-kind determinant proves that the part of the common gcd coprime to the cyclotomic clearing value divides 3^n+2^n, confining every possible quadratic repair to clearing-supported prime powers. Exact counterexamples show that those primes need not have order <=2n, and the stronger valuation bound v_ell(G)<=v_ell(D_M)+v_ell(3^n+2^n) already fails at (n,m,ell)=(4,16,7). On the fixed diagonal m=n, all odd row content divides the specialization-independent resultant Res_p(A_n,C_n). Its cyclotomic local factors now have an authored all-index q-Lucas product law: for n=ar+b the previously missing norm is the smaller diagonal P_b(p^b), multiplied by an explicit harmonic scalar. The exact cross and harmonic factors consume about 0.55015 of the 0.76546 quadratic budget, but the smaller-diagonal product drives the clearing resultant above budget already at n=15, before the P-Q factor. Thus full-resultant height is closed as a scalar content bound; only a specialization-selective gcd theorem strictly below that resultant remains on this diagonal. Inward evaluations require a new exact target identity, and higher-rank multiple-q-Jacobi systems remain outside this result. For Zudilin's cubic Hankel route, normalized q-order, scalar content, and entry-valuation border charge are all sharply insufficient; rank five has precisely the forced non-p content Phi_1^3 Phi_2. The all-d wrapped-Hankel resultant proof now shows that the full first-appearance associated-graded cyclotomic residue is nonzero for every d, eliminating cancellation among minimum-order first-appearance terms and killing the expanding homogeneous boundary mode. This supplies no extra cumulative cubic charge. A surviving Hankel route must create higher-valuation-layer cancellation of cubic density, a genuinely global norm or resultant gain beyond the first block, or a different integral model. No irrationality theorem for 3/2 or universal rational-base theorem is established. The step-1 window-divisor predicate has now been evaluated for the first time: every start in the cofinality half of the tested range carries a divisor across the exact window of width 3s^2+5s+3, and every newly appearing prime divides 3^s-2^s at its first start, seven out of seven. Step 1 is therefore not the weak link, and the residual is a comparison of ord_p(3/2) against the quadratic window rather than a further change of target. Step 1 of the three-halves producer is therefore closed by a fixed prime rather than a moving one, and hypothesis (H) of the Casoratian block-law derivation is false at p=5 (three residues mod 25) and is replaced by the true and sufficient 5-adic continuity (C5), which follows from the certified monodromy R_(j+P_N) = -R_j mod 5^N. Height and decay are untouched and no irrationality theorem at 3/2 is established. HOMOGENISATION CEILING (2026-08-24): the content lane is now capped by a base-only inequality. The two homogenised numerators are coprime (gcd = 1 exactly at every tested index) and the Casoratian bounds any shared content by 3^j(3^j+2^(j+1)), i.e. O(j), so no gcd theorem can move the quadratic constant. Since B_j is a multiple of num(R_j) = a^(D_j+O(j)) and decay needs log B_j < 2 D_j log(a/b), decay requires a > b^2 with the degree exponent cancelling. At 3/2 the irreducible floor (3/2)log3 j^2 = 1.64792 j^2 already exceeds the 1.21640 j^2 budget before any clearing is counted. Restoring the clearing derives the recorded threshold log b/log a < 1/2 - 1/pi^2 exactly and identifies 1/pi^2 as the cyclotomic sum. Therefore the primitive-content and Padé-height producers cannot reach 3/2 at any level of success; their maximum prize is the band b^2 < a with log b/log a >= 1/2 - 1/pi^2, smallest member 5/2. 3/2 requires congruence-constrained or higher-rank construction instead. RANK BUDGET LAW (2026-08-24): a rank-r type-I system closes a/b only if log b/log a < (r-1-kappa)/r with kappa the per-degree clearing rate, measured at rank two as 2/pi^2. At r=2 this reproduces the recorded threshold 1/2 - 1/pi^2 to twelve digits and identifies its halves as homogenisation and the phi-sum. Rank needed: 2 for integer q and 7/2, 3 for 5/2 and 10/3, FOUR for 3/2, 6 for 4/3, 9 for 5/4. So 3/2 is the first explicit base beyond rank two even with perfect content, and beyond rank three at the observed clearing rate - it misses rank three by 0.03181 in t and clears rank four by 0.06841. Closing 3/2 therefore requires either rank three with kappa_3 < 0.10721 (53% of the rank-two rate) or rank four at the observed rate, the latter being Zudilin's cubic Hankel construction, which is already the right rank. This is a necessary-condition budget, not a construction, and it does not address non-vanishing of the constructed form, which is the real high-rank obstruction.

hypothesis.statement: For cofinally many starts s a moving divisor exists across the exact window of width 3s^2 + 5s + 3, and each newly appearing prime divides the source denominator 3^s - 2^s at its first start.

probe.question: Does the step-1 predicate hold start by start, and is the divisor source-supported in the first-appearance sense?
probe.computation: Build the primitive q-Apery rows from the exact Fraction recurrence to index 677, take the gcd of the denominator coordinates across each exact window [s, s + 3s^2 + 5s + 3], factor it, and test each newly appearing prime against 3^s - 2^s. The row generator is anchored against the prior lab's 211 | B_j for 5 <= j <= 255.
probe.falsifier: A start whose window gcd is 1. If such starts are cofinal, step 1 as stated is false and the target must change again.
probe.stop_condition: Cofinal empty windows retire step 1; the probe deliberately does not extend the row cutoff hunting for new tail primes, which the prior lab states would not change the mathematical status.

analytic_bridge.survival_consequence: Step 1 is not the weak link: the residual on this route is a proof of what the computation shows rather than another change of target.
analytic_bridge.falsification_consequence: The window formulation joins the fixed-tail formulation as refuted, and the route needs a third target.

result.summary: 677 rows; starts 0..14. Only s = 0, 1, 2, 4 have window gcd 1 - the earliest starts - and every start in the upper half of the range carries a divisor, which is where cofinality lives. The divisor set grows with s: 19 at s=3, 211 at s=5, 71*211 at s=7, +1009 at s=9, +331 at s=11, +29927 at s=13, +463 at s=14. The source-support law is exact on first appearance, seven out of seven: 19|19, 211|211, 71|2059, 1009|19171, 331|175099, 29927|1586131, 463|4766585.

progress.decision_basis: Every start in the cofinality half carries a divisor, and every newly appearing prime divides 3^s - 2^s at its first start.
progress.next_analytic_target: Show that for every large s the prime p_s dividing 3^s - 2^s selected at first appearance has no loss block meeting [s, s + 3s^2 + 5s + 3] - a comparison of ord_p(3/2) against a quadratic window.
